section_summary: This section combines reports on suspected Japanese commercial, propaganda, and espionage activity with extensive correspondence about Japanese-language schools, churches, and the loyalties of Japanese Americans on the Pacific Coast. It includes an embassy despatch on Japanese propaganda, three letters from Marguerite I. Smith, press clippings concerning Japanese finance and naval surveillance, and numerous State Department–FBI acknowledgments concerning individual espionage cases. The later pages document interagency circulation of reports about Ryoichi Hara, Japanese dual citizenship, alleged spy rings, and possible Japanese consular or military personnel.

subfiles.title: Cover letter forwarding a supplementary report on C. T. Takahashi
subfiles.about: Forwards Post Office Inspector Morse's supplementary report on Seattle resident C. T. Takahashi.
subfiles.summary: Bannerman submits Inspector Morse's February 7, 1939 supplementary report on C. T. Takahashi, following his February 6 Seattle report.

subfiles.title: Supplementary report on C. T. Takahashi
subfiles.about: Reports commercial and personal information concerning Seattle importer C. T. Takahashi.
subfiles.summary: Morse says Takahashi had possible connections with a British-managed import-export firm in Shanghai and conducted transactions involving scrap iron, ores, and Japanese letters of credit. Seattle merchants regarded him as unreliable, tricky, talkative, and unscrupulous, while much of his current business was believed to be handled by associates in California.

subfiles.title: Digest of Tokyo despatch no. 3888
subfiles.about: Summarizes an embassy despatch about a Japanese official's assessment of propaganda in the United States.
subfiles.summary: Digest of Tokyo despatch no. 3888: an official believes Japanese propaganda is not as inept as asserted; the despatch need not be read.

subfiles.title: Statement of Foreign Office Official Regarding Japanese Propaganda in the United States
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits a translated Asahi Shimbun article reporting Jun Tsuchiya's views on Japanese publicity in America.
subfiles.summary: Grew forwards an article about Jun Tsuchiya's return from a Foreign Office publicity mission to the United States. The despatch highlights Tsuchiya's conclusion that Japanese propaganda was more effective than generally believed.

subfiles.title: Japan Not Necessarily Inapt at Propaganda, Foreign Office Official Back from America Says
subfiles.about: Presents Jun Tsuchiya's observations from a Japanese publicity tour of the United States.
subfiles.summary: Translated article: Foreign Office official Tsuchiya says Japan should stress its consistent imperial policy, praises Japanese world's-fair pavilions, and describes failing to change March of Time's Japan film.

subfiles.title: Analysis of Mrs. Smith's observations
subfiles.about: Evaluates Marguerite Smith's proposals concerning Japanese propaganda and foreign-language schools.
subfiles.summary: Memorandum calls Mrs. Smith perceptive; she proposes American-born teachers for foreign-language schools and sees integration of American-born Japanese as the lasting solution; recommends only an acknowledgment.

subfiles.title: Letter on Japanese-language schools and assimilation
subfiles.about: Urges regulation of Japanese-language schools while arguing that American-born Japanese should be socially accepted and assimilated.
subfiles.summary: Smith urges requiring American-born citizens to teach in foreign-language schools and asks Welles to share her views with Martin Dies anonymously, arguing prejudice drives second-generation Japanese toward Japan.

subfiles.title: Considers New Alien Laws
subfiles.about: Reports proposed federal legislation targeting extremist organizations and alien supporters.
subfiles.summary: Clipping: Martin Dies considers licensing groups advocating intolerance and mandatory deportation of alien advocates of sedition.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Smith's February letter
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Smith's further comments about the Japanese population in her community.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton thanks Smith for her frank letter, promises continued study, and says her identity will not be disclosed.

subfiles.title: Under Secretary's referral of Smith's first letter
subfiles.to: Stanley K. Hornbeck and Maxwell M. Hamilton
subfiles.about: Requests an assessment and acknowledgment of Smith's confidential letter.
subfiles.summary: Welles asks Hornbeck his view of the attached letter and directs that it be acknowledged after consultation.

subfiles.title: Confidential letter on Japanese-American residents
subfiles.about: Alleges that Japanese schools and churches in Santa Maria spread pro-Japanese propaganda among second-generation youth.
subfiles.summary: Drawing on four years as a Sunday-school teacher at a Japanese Union Christian Church, Smith describes propaganda about the war in China, her removal from a class of older boys, and the influence of the Japanese minister and language school. She portrays the community as tightly organized and loyal to Japan, urges federal control or abolition of foreign-language schools and periodicals, and insists that her identity remain confidential because she fears retaliation.

subfiles.title: Reply to Smith concerning foreign-agent registration
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Smith's first letter and asks for information that might support action under the Foreign Agents Registration Act.
subfiles.summary: Welles says Smith's observations as a Sunday-school teacher are of interest and will receive careful attention. He asks for the Japanese pastor's name and address so the Department might call the registration requirements for agents of foreign principals to his attention, while promising to protect Smith's identity.

subfiles.title: Assessment of Smith's third letter
subfiles.about: Recommends a restrained response to Marguerite Smith's third letter.
subfiles.summary: Memorandum finds Smith's third letter largely repetitive and recommends a reply by Hamilton that does not encourage more letters.

subfiles.title: Under Secretary's referral of Smith's third letter
subfiles.to: Stanley K. Hornbeck and Maxwell M. Hamilton
subfiles.about: Requests an appropriate acknowledgment of another letter from Mrs. Smith.
subfiles.summary: Welles forwards a further letter from Smith of Santa Maria, asking Far Eastern Affairs to draft an acknowledgment.

subfiles.title: Third confidential letter on Japanese-American residents
subfiles.about: Warns that Japanese propaganda and financial ambitions pose a danger to the United States and urges denial of American financing to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Smith recounts an angry exchange with a Japanese American employee and attributes the woman's reaction to Tokyo-controlled news and community indoctrination. Citing James A. B. Scherer and Ralph Reiner, she argues that Japanese militarists seek expansion and asks Welles to consult Henry Morgenthau to prevent Japan from obtaining American money. She again describes second-generation Japanese as trapped between American exclusion and pressure from elders, schools, and churches.

subfiles.title: Japan Seeks War Funds in U.S.
subfiles.about: Reports the establishment of a Japanese finance mission seeking American loans.
subfiles.summary: Clipping: Japan created its first official finance mission in the U.S. to fund occupied China and continue the war, tied to a proposed bloc with Manchukuo and China.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Smith's May 22 letter
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Smith's additional views on American-Japanese relations.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton, at Welles's request, acknowledges Smith's May 22 letter, finding her information of interest and appreciating her motivation.

subfiles.title: 1957 FBI return note
subfiles.about: Records the return of an unidentified letter and enclosures to the FBI through the Office of Security.
subfiles.summary: 1957 note: the item under the referenced file number was returned to the FBI through the Office of Security on July 1, 1957.

subfiles.summary: Messersmith thanks Hoover for his June 2 letter on the case Takahisa Hattori; Jiro Takeda, Espionage.

subfiles.title: Inquiry concerning Shiro Omachi

subfiles.summary: Messersmith thanks Hoover for the June 13 letter and enclosed report. The FBI case is identified as Shiro Omachi, Espionage.

subfiles.title: Charge-out record for file material

subfiles.summary: Charge-out record with unclear annotations dated September 27, 1955 and March 27, 1957 about file custody.

subfiles.title: Report of Ryoichi Hara's desertion
subfiles.about: Reports that Japanese engineer Ryoichi Hara deserted his ship in Brooklyn and might be a spy.
subfiles.summary: New York police report that Ryoichi Hara, engineer of the SS Yamacoto Maru, left the ship June 14 and vanished; the squad suspected espionage, and State's special agent forwarded the details.

subfiles.title: Naval Intelligence memorandum on Ryoichi Hara
subfiles.to: Commander Nixon, Office of Naval Intelligence
subfiles.about: Passes the report of Ryoichi Hara's desertion and possible espionage to Naval Intelligence.
subfiles.summary: Naval Intelligence memorandum quoting the Alien Squad's report on Hara's disappearance; copies to Military Intelligence and the FBI.

subfiles.title: Military Intelligence memorandum on Ryoichi Hara
subfiles.about: Passes the report of Ryoichi Hara's desertion and possible espionage to Military Intelligence.
subfiles.summary: Military Intelligence memorandum reproducing the Alien Squad information on Hara's disappearance in Brooklyn; copies to Naval Intelligence and the FBI.

subfiles.title: FBI memorandum on Ryoichi Hara
subfiles.about: Passes the report of Ryoichi Hara's desertion and possible espionage to the FBI.
subfiles.summary: FBI memorandum quoting the police report on Hara, his ship and his disappearance in Brooklyn; copies to Military and Naval Intelligence.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding a newspaper clipping on a Japanese ship
subfiles.about: Forwards a newspaper clipping that Kramer believes Warren will find interesting.
subfiles.summary: Kramer explains his messenger had left before he sent a clipping about a Japanese ship, calling it interesting.

subfiles.title: Japanese Ship Caught by Navy
subfiles.about: Reports the discovery of a Japanese trawler near the Navy's restricted San Clemente Island training area.
subfiles.summary: Clipping: naval officers suspicious after a Japanese fishing vessel was found in prohibited waters near the fleet's secret base, recalling a Japanese liner near Los Angeles Harbor; unrelated fragments also appear.

subfiles.title: File-number divider 894.20211/246

subfiles.summary: Far Eastern Affairs finds no information on the person in the FBI case, identified as Syoiti Morihira and aliases.

subfiles.title: Assistant Secretary's routing note on Morihira
subfiles.about: Directs careful review of the FBI communication concerning Morihira.
subfiles.summary: Assistant Secretary's handwritten note asking that the Morihira case be examined carefully and routed for remarks; poor OCR.

subfiles.summary: Messersmith thanks Hoover for the June 29 report on S. Morihira, alias Mariharia; Espionage, and asks for copies of further information.

subfiles.summary: Messersmith thanks Hoover for Louis Wine's June 15 report in the Sehei Ono espionage case and asks for any additional reports.

subfiles.title: File-number divider 894.20211/249

subfiles.summary: File-number divider 894.20211/249 with no associated document.

subfiles.summary: Messersmith acknowledges Hoover's July 5 letter with information on Japanese dual citizenship and espionage.

subfiles.summary: Warren, for Messersmith, acknowledges Hoover's July 11 letter on the continuing FBI case on Japanese dual citizenship and espionage.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment concerning Jesse S. Shima and a Japanese spy ring
subfiles.about: Acknowledges a further FBI report on Jesse S. Shima and an alleged Japanese spy ring.
subfiles.summary: Warren thanks Hoover for the July 26 report in the Jesse Shima case and asks for additional information on the alleged spy ring.

subfiles.title: File-number divider 894.20211/255
subfiles.about: Marks file item 894.20211/255 associated with the following handwritten letter.
subfiles.summary: File-number divider 894.20211/255 preceding a degraded handwritten communication on alleged Japanese and German agents.

subfiles.title: Handwritten letter alleging Japanese and German agent headquarters
subfiles.about: Makes poorly legible allegations about Japanese Army personnel, German Nazi or Bund agents, and headquarters in New York.
subfiles.summary: The heavily degraded text appears to describe a search of the New York telephone directory, a call to purported Japanese Army headquarters, and claims about Japanese officers or flyers. It also mentions an informant from Boston, reports allegedly sent to Edgar Hoover about a German Nazi agent, the German-American Bund, criticism of the President, and concern about tolerating foreign activity in the United States.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference note on Alberti Duarte Rauromet's statement
subfiles.about: Cross-references a statement alleging that Japanese moved between ocean liners and fishing boats to observe United States warship movements.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Alberti Duarte Rauromet claims he repeatedly saw two Japanese move from liners to fishing boats to gather naval information, per Monterrey despatch no. 69.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about alleged Japanese consular personnel
subfiles.to: Salisbury, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Asks whether individuals named in an FBI letter were attached to the Japanese Consulate in San Francisco.
subfiles.summary: Memorandum asks Salisbury whether persons in an FBI letter were Japanese consular staff; Personnel found no record of them.

subfiles.title: Personnel Division response on alleged consular personnel
subfiles.about: Reports that the Personnel Division has no records concerning the individuals under inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Jones reports the Personnel Division has no record of the persons named.
